criteria.passage: I’d gather updates from both the site manager and the contractor and compare them with the repair plan so I can understand what has been completed and what is still pending. I’d ask for the latest view on the parts shortage, any workaround being considered, and whether either party sees a risk to the completion date.
criteria.rationale: The answer clearly identifies multiple monitoring inputs needed to track execution: updates from both parties, comparison against the repair plan, status of completed/pending work, parts shortage information, workaround status, and perceived risk to the completion date.

criteria.passage: If the delay starts to look more serious, I’d make sure it is brought to the attention of the appropriate lead and that the next shift has the latest information.
criteria.rationale: The candidate explicitly recognizes a condition under which action is needed: when the delay appears to be becoming more serious. This shows awareness of a deviation threshold that triggers response.

criteria.passage: I’d make sure it is brought to the attention of the appropriate lead and that the next shift has the latest information. I’d also keep checking in until I had a clearer picture of whether the repair was still on track.
criteria.rationale: The response includes escalation to the appropriate lead, handoff of current information to the next shift, and continued follow-up by checking in until the status is clear, which demonstrates escalation and follow-through.
